ITEM.PTXT: As before, MacPherson strut type suspension with L-shaped lower arms is adopted.
With the adoption of the 2GR-FE engine, the suspension geometry has been optimized, achieving a high level of handling, stability and ride comfort.
The steering gear box is mounted directly to the suspension member, improving the feeling of rigidity during initial steering operation.
An integrated input type upper support has been adopted. The rebound stopper plate construction improves the initial effectiveness of the shock absorber damping force on the rebound side.
A urethane bound stopper has been adopted, providing soft non-linear characteristics at initial contact and achieving both roll rigidity during cornering and a supple ride.

A side force reduction spring has been adopted to control the reaction force line of the coil spring and reduce the bending force on the shock absorber, reducing suspension friction and achieving an excellent ride.
An upper insulator with an integrated dust cover has been adopted.
A compact, lightweight inner diameter restraint type upper spring seat has been adopted.
Low-pressure gas (N2) filled shock absorbers with linear control valves have been adopted, achieving a high level of handling, stability and ride comfort.

The piston valve used in the shock absorber has been enlarged, and a laminated construction has been adopted for the rear valve so that damping force can be generated even during the compression stroke. As a result, compared with a construction in which damping force is generated only by the base valve during the compression stroke, damping force is generated from a lower speed range, achieving a high-quality ride.

The linear control valve uses laminated valves to create a choke construction (a construction that greatly changes the direction of oil flow through the orifice), achieving linear damping force in the low speed range. The rear valve, which conventionally served as a check valve, has also been redesigned into a laminated valve with a choke construction.
Lower damping force in the medium to high speed range is achieved by reducing the valve rigidity of the leaf valve.
Damping force changes are generated from the extremely low piston speed range, making vehicle behavior in response to steering operation, etc. gentle and achieving excellent handling and stability.
Lowering the damping force in the medium to high speed range reduces vehicle vibration caused by road surface irregularities, ensuring a supple ride.
An L-shaped lower arm has been adopted. The arm shape has been optimized to achieve both high rigidity and light weight.
The size of the No.2 bushing has been increased. As a result, longitudinal compliance has been increased, contributing to improved harshness.
A front stabilizer is provided as standard on all models to ensure sufficient roll rigidity.

Ball joint type stabilizer links are used. By attaching them to the shock absorbers, responsiveness from the initial stage of roll is increased and the stabilizer effect is improved, achieving both steering stability and ride comfort.
A pressed steel plate suspension member is used.
